summary: myidsan gains generic OpenID Connect (OIDC) login as a relying party (Phase 3 of docs/MYIDSAN_ENTERPRISE_SSO_PLAN.md), so it can federate against any spec-compliant enterprise IdP (Keycloak, Authentik, ADFS, Entra, ...) without a bespoke integration per provider. A new login.oidc[] config array (infra/login/login_models.go's OidcProviderConfigModel: key, display_name, issuer_url, client_id/secret, redirect_url, scopes, ca_cert_path, groups_claim, insecure_skip_email_verified) drives infra/login/oidc.go (github.com/coreos/go-oidc/v3, a thin layer over the already-vendored golang.org/x/oauth2): NewOidcLogin runs OIDC discovery against the issuer at startup (10s timeout, optional pinned CA for private-CA intranet IdPs) and builds an infra/login.RedirectProvider per configured entry, so GET /api/login/{key} and GET /api/callback/{key} work exactly like Google/GitHub. The login leg runs PKCE (S256) plus a nonce, both riding single-use HttpOnly cookies scoped to the callback path (mirroring the existing state-cookie pattern); the callback verifies the id_token against the discovered JWKS, checks the nonce, and maps claims via the exported/unit-tested OidcIdentityFromClaims: an explicit email_verified=false is refused unless the per-provider override is set (an absent claim is accepted), and groups_claim feeds Identity.Groups from either a JSON array or ADFS's bare-string shape. Accounts bind to "oidc:<key>" (Identity.Provider) - changing an entry's key orphans existing federated accounts, called out in the config doc comment. infra/login/provider.go's BuildRegistry registers each configured entry only when client_id/client_secret are present and discovery succeeds; either failure (typo'd issuer, IdP down at boot, bad CA) logs a WARNING and skips just that provider, the same fail-soft policy Google/GitHub/Kerberos already use - the rest of the login page is unaffected and it comes back on the next restart. "ldap" and "kerberos" were added to the registry's reserved-key set so an operator-chosen OIDC key can never shadow either fixed route. infra/apphost/run.go's applySensitiveConfig now supports per-provider client-secret env overrides, OIDC_<KEY>_CLIENT_SECRET (key upper-cased, non-alphanumerics mapped to underscore, e.g. corp-idp -> OIDC_CORP_IDP_CLIENT_SECRET). apps/myidsan/services/directory.go gains AdmitExternalIdentity: it wraps UpsertFederated with group->role seeding from FederatedGroupMapping rows scoped to the login's exact provider string, always non-authoritative regardless of the directory's own Authoritative toggle - a mapping only seeds a still-pending account's role once, never re-applies on every login, because an external IdP's groups claim is only ever as fresh as the last login's id_token (unlike LDAP, which myidsan can query for live group truth). This works with the directory itself disabled, since mappings are provider-scoped rows, not directory settings. apps/myidsan/apis/login.go's providerCallback now routes through a new admitRedirectIdentity helper that calls AdmitExternalIdentity when a directory service is wired, falling back to plain UpsertFederated otherwise; social logins are unaffected since they carry no groups. The Federation -> Directory group-mapping editor in the SPA gained an editable Provider field (default "ldap", e.g. "oidc:keycloak") and a Provider column in the mappings table, so OIDC group mappings can be entered alongside LDAP ones.
compatibility: Backward compatible: login.oidc defaults to an empty array in both apps/myidsan/config.json and config.dev.json, so existing installs see no new login button, no discovery calls, and no behavior change until an operator adds an entry and supplies a client id/secret. A half-configured or unreachable OIDC entry is skipped with a startup warning rather than failing boot, matching the existing Google/GitHub/Kerberos degrade-gracefully policy. Existing LDAP/Kerberos/social login flows, the FederatedGroupMapping schema, and UpsertFederated's strict (provider, subject) account matching are all unchanged; AdmitExternalIdentity is purely additive on top of them. Adding "ldap"/"kerberos" to the registry's reserved-key set is a no-op for existing config, since neither was ever a valid registry provider key. Verified live on a fresh sqlite boot: a bogus-issuer OIDC entry logs a WARNING and is skipped while google/ldap/kerberos remain in the providers list; local login is unaffected. The full authorization-code round trip against a real IdP (Keycloak) is not yet exercised - noted alongside LDAP/Kerberos as needing a live bench test, which the user will run separately.
